bad.why: It means discussion is shut down, the opposite of a free exchange. Say jiyuu ni or enryo naku.

bad.s: 授業中[じゅぎょうちゅう]、先生[せんせい]に{問答無用[もんどうむよう]}な質問[しつもん]をしてしまった。
bad.en: (meant: I asked the teacher a pointless question in class)
bad.why: It does not mean 'a useless question'; it describes refusing to discuss at all. Say tsumaranai shitsumon or muda na shitsumon.

lit: great nerve, treating no enemy as worth fearing

use.how: 大胆不敵な犯行 / 笑み / 手口, 大胆不敵にも: said of a person or act showing brazen daring in the face of danger or a strong opponent, often a criminal or a challenger.

near.diff: 傍若無人 is rude disregard for the people around you; 大胆不敵 is fearless daring in the face of danger or a strong opponent.

cue: A thief sends the museum a note naming the night he will steal the painting, then takes it right under the guards' noses.

ctx.s: 「あの怪盗[かいとう]、予告状[よこくじょう]まで出[だ]すなんて{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}だね。」
ctx.en: "That phantom thief even sends a warning note first. What nerve!"

ctx.s: 挑戦者[ちょうせんしゃ]は王者[おうじゃ]を前[まえ]にしても、{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}な笑[え]みを浮[う]かべていた。
ctx.en: Even face to face with the champion, the challenger wore a fearless smile.

ctx.s: 犯人[はんにん]は{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}にも、真昼[まひる]の銀行[ぎんこう]に押[お]し入[い]った。
ctx.en: The robber had the audacity to break into a bank in broad daylight.

ctx.s: 無名[むめい]の新人[しんじん]が、横綱[よこづな]に正面[しょうめん]からぶつかっていく{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}な相撲[すもう]を見[み]せた。
ctx.en: An unknown newcomer fought fearlessly, charging head-on at the grand champion.

ctx.s: 警備員[けいびいん]の目[め]の前[まえ]で絵[え]をすり替[か]えるという{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}な手口[てぐち]に、警察[けいさつ]も驚[おどろ]いた。
ctx.en: Even the police were startled by the brazen method: swapping the painting right in front of the guards.

ctx.s: その小説[しょうせつ]の主人公[しゅじんこう]は、{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}で口[くち]の悪[わる]い女[おんな]スパイだ。
ctx.en: The novel's heroine is a fearless, sharp-tongued spy.

bad.s: このチームは{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}で、今季[こんき]は一度[いちど]も負[ま]けていない。
bad.en: (meant: this team is unbeatable and hasn't lost once this season)
bad.why: Futeki means fearless of an enemy, not having no rival. For unbeaten or invincible say muteki.

bad.s: 兄[あに]は{大胆不敵[だいたんふてき]}で、よく財布[さいふ]を家[いえ]に忘[わす]れる。
bad.en: (meant: my brother is careless and often leaves his wallet at home)
bad.why: It means fearless daring in the face of danger or an opponent, not careless or easygoing. Say ukkari shite ite or ukkarimono de.
